purpose: Reusable multi-turn browser journeys for the retained ConnectedConcierge SDK path.

requestAccounting.shopperTurns: derived from scenario turns actually sent
requestAccounting.completionRequests: all observed /api/chat calls including continuation, retry and failed responses
requestAccounting.auxiliaries: classifier and suggestion calls are unknown unless separately observable
requestAccounting.maximumCompletionRequests: must be set explicitly before a live run; never inferred from shopper-turn count

evidenceModes.live: Assertions use rendered UI state and observed SDK/API transport without prescribing assistant wording.
evidenceModes.fixture: Adverse evidence is injected only by an explicitly named route fixture; it is never presented as live evidence.

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: My sister's birthday is coming up and I want something she can wear anywhere. I can spend no more than 250 dollars on it.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: Swaps 'under $250' for 'no more than 250', an inclusive ceiling. Adverse because exactly-250 items qualify under this wording, so retrieval and assessment must preserve inclusive boundary semantics instead of normalizing to 'under'.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: Hold on, I think I misled myself earlier. It really has to land below 150 all in. Please look at my saved options again with that correction.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: Frames the budget correction as the shopper's own earlier mistake rather than a new rule, and 'all in' implies a combined basis. Adverse because it tests mid-flow correction: comparison must refresh without resetting the brief or re-running intake.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: The earrings are not doing it for me. Could we try something more understated for the ears? The necklace stays as it is.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: Drops both the explicit product form (studs) and the measurable property (lightweight), leaving a vague component reference plus a restated anchor. Adverse because the agent must resolve the replacement from context without inventing a weight claim or dropping the anchor.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: Thank you, this is plenty to go on for now. I may come back to it another day.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: A polite soft stop with a hinted return and no imperative word like stop. Adverse because suggestions or further searches after it violate stopping-respected, while a cold goodbye reply would misread the rapport the playbook asks for.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: What else have you got that might work for him? I would like to see how they differ, side by side.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: Removes the explicit count ('two meaningful alternatives') and the word compare, replacing them with an open request plus a side-by-side hint. Adverse because the agent must choose bounded curation itself and recognize comparison intent without keyword echoing.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

wordingVariantsDeclared.variantText: Sorry, where were we? It was those two necklaces from earlier, and one of them had a detail I liked but I cannot remember which.
wordingVariantsDeclared.whyAdverseOrVaried: Turns the crisp 'Back to those two' into a delayed resumption with admitted memory loss and a partial detail. Adverse because the agent must restore the exact same two identities from stable references without restarting intake, re-listing fresh products, or guessing which detail the shopper means.
wordingVariantsDeclared.mode: reserved; runs only with JTV_WORDING_VARIANTS=1 and consumes the same budget

connectedSlices.purpose: Bounded connected slice proving the replacement path end to end: accepted anchor preserved across a component swap, yellow-gold exclusion upheld, exact cents subtotal with unknowns withheld, guardrail withholding on a conflicting look, and a visible committed look after the swap.
connectedSlices.launchGate: Requires Controller slot handback, Claude 1 C4 verified (landed per PLAN-3.1-STATUS Stage 3 row), Dev2 Stage 5 stability, and an explicit per-slice completion budget.

budgetReservation.basis: 8 shopper turns at roughly 2 requests per turn plus retry reserve; derives from the same continuation accounting as the Stage 7 cap

adverseEvidenceFixtures.condition: A selected stud record has no weight field.
Structured material says white gold while description says plated treatment.
A packaged set omits a required component in the returned evidence.
Optional blog retrieval times out while product evidence remains available.

turns.text: I need a birthday gift for my sister, something versatile under $250.
Show me at least five varied choices so I can save the ones I like.
I saved five. Compare these two and help me narrow them down.
I am browsing for a gift and do not know whether vermeil or solid gold is the better fit.
Can you explain the difference briefly, then show suitable options?
One listing says gold but I cannot tell whether the treatment is verified.
That is enough for now. Stop showing alternatives.
I am shopping for my partner. Find a sapphire necklace in white gold for a complete look under $700.
I like the necklace you showed. Build a look around it.
Keep the necklace, but replace the earrings with lightweight studs.
The studs may be missing weight information. Check that rather than guessing.
Find a pearl necklace for my mother, under $300. Sapphire is only required for the necklace if it comes up later.
Compare two exact necklaces.
Before deciding, what care question matters for pearls? Give me more detail.
Back to those two.
I need a ring gift for a friend, around $180, and she likes blue stones.
Show me options and save the two I mention.
Actually, the budget is strictly under $150. Compare the saved options again.
The second one, but cheaper.
Help me compare a ring set with separate pieces for an anniversary gift.
The set might not include the matching band. Verify its contents before calling it complete.
Use the separate ring as the anchor and show one feasible look.
Choose the stronger option and stop.
Find a bracelet for a graduation gift, silver tone, under $220.
Show me at least five possibilities so I can save the ones I like.
Compare these two saved pieces and keep the best anchor.
Build a look, then replace the companion piece with something less expensive.
I want a bracelet for everyday wear but I am unsure how to care for one with a pearl.
Answer the care question from the available guidance, then keep browsing.
If the product record does not establish treatment, leave that unknown.
I have enough choices. Stop.
Find a watch gift for my dad, under $400, with a simple face.
Show me two meaningful alternatives and compare them.
Which one is better for the stated priorities? Keep the reason tied to the records.
Save the winner and stop showing more.
I already like this watch. Find a complementary bracelet for a complete look under $500 total.
Keep the watch and replace the bracelet with a different material.
If compatibility is not established, say so clearly and keep the item available for consideration.
That is the one. Stop.

scenarios.purpose: E21 long continuity case: at least 22 shopper turns where the full scoped brief, accepted components and stable references survive with no repeated intake and no cumulative drift.

turns.text: Our tenth anniversary is coming up and I want to mark it with a piece of jewelry for my wife.
She wears white gold and loves sapphires. Please keep the whole budget at $900.
Start with a ring and show me what you have.
Let me save several of these as we go.
One correction: sapphire matters most to her, diamonds would only be a bonus.
While you keep looking, how durable is a sapphire for everyday wear?
Good, now back to finding the ring.
Show me five fresh possibilities so I can add to my saved list.
I have my favorites saved. Put the first two side by side.
Between these two, which one fits her taste better?
New information: the total spend has to stay strictly under $800, not $900.
Set the pricier one aside and find me a similar ring that fits the tighter budget.
Show those two rings together again under the new limit.
What actually differs between the two sapphires in front of me?
I should mention she is quite hard on her jewelry day to day.
Given everything I told you, which of the two would you stand behind?
Good choice. Save that one for us.
Could we add matching earrings so it becomes a little set?
Those earrings look heavy. Swap them for something lighter, like small studs.
Does the set truly include every piece shown? Please verify rather than assume.
This is the one we want. We will go with the ring.
That covers it. Please stop showing me alternatives now.
Hi there. My mum turns 60 next month and I would love to find her a piece of jewelry she will actually wear.
I keep coming back to earrings for her, and everything together should stay at or under 200 dollars.
Show me a good spread of styles so I can pick out the ones I like.
These three at the top feel like the strongest candidates. What really separates them?
Of those, the middle one keeps catching my eye. Would you stand behind it for her?
Good, let's call that the one. No need to show me anything else today.
I have been trying to pick out something pearl for my aunt as a thank you gift, but I am honestly lost on the difference between the pearl types.
Could you walk me through it simply? Just the parts that would actually change what I buy.
That helps. Now, could you show me some pearl pieces that could work for her? I would rather stay at 180 dollars or below.
A few of these appeal to me. Let me hold onto them while I think.
One thing: if a listing does not say whether a pearl has been treated, please leave that as unknown instead of filling it in.
This has been genuinely useful. I have what I need, so you can stop there.
I have a wedding to attend in a few weeks and I want a necklace with earrings that read as one considered look.
For both pieces together I would like to keep the whole thing under 350 dollars.
Let's begin with the necklace. That first style you showed feels right as the centre of the look, so I will keep it.
Now what earrings would sit well with it?
Two of those could work. I will hold them so I can weigh them against each other.
Put the first two saved pieces together as the set and show me what the total comes to.
Yes, that combination works for me. That is all I need for today, so no more suggestions please.
